title: AEO Institutional Framework and Operational Integration
summary: The concept of 'customs offices' evolves from a general administrative entity to a specialized, integrated network under the Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) framework. Over time, the role of the 'AEO Center' is formalized as the central authority, while other customs offices are increasingly mandated to provide prioritized services, data sharing, and operational support to AEO-certified entities.

evolution.institutional_role: From general customs administration to a centralized AEO-centric coordination model.
evolution.operational_scope: Shift from passive compliance to active, prioritized service delivery for certified operators.
evolution.procedural_integration: Introduction of standardized reporting templates and cross-departmental data sharing protocols.

timeline.change: Formal establishment of the AEO Center and definition of its oversight role over other customs offices.
Expansion of operational mandates for customs offices, including mandatory priority processing, data reporting, and issuance of special access credentials.
Minor linguistic refinement of the AEO Center's mandate.
Refinement of definitions and procedural scope for the AEO Center.

Authorized Economic Operator: An Authorized Economic Operator is defined as an entity that has been granted recognition certification in accordance with the specified rules.
This is the designated regulatory agency responsible for monitoring, though other customs offices may act as monitoring agencies within their respective jurisdictions for certified entities.
Customs Act 2023: The Act is formally defined as the Customs Act 2023 (Act No. 57 of 2023).
Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Commi: The Committee refers to the specific oversight body designated in the rules for handling matters related to authorized economic operators.
Customs Officer: A Customs Officer is defined as any official appointed under Section 4 of the Customs Act 2023.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is defined as the National Board of Revenue established under the National Board of Revenue Order, 1972.
Logistics Operator: A Logistics Operator is a service provider involved in the customs process, such as a customs agent, shipping agent, freight forwarder, terminal operator, or courier service provider.
Affiliated Institution: This term encompasses businesses or companies linked to the same ownership, partnership, or directorship, including cases where individuals serve as chairmen or directors across multiple entities.
Provisional Certificate: A Provisional Certificate is a time-bound certification issued by the Committee subject to the fulfillment of specific conditions.
Recognition Certificate: A Recognition Certificate is the formal accreditation issued under the relevant rules for authorized economic operators.

National Board of Revenue: The Board is responsible for establishing the Authorized Economic Operator Center, including appointing a Director General from among its senior officers.
The Board is supported by the Center in coordinating mutual recognition agreements with other countries and in formulating policies and strategies regarding Authorized Economic Operators.
Authorized Economic Operator: The Center is formed by the Board to manage the recognition process, auditing, monitoring, and compliance of Authorized Economic Operators.
It acts as a liaison between customs offices and stakeholders to facilitate trade and ensure the effective implementation of authorized operations.
Until the formal establishment of the Center, its functions are to be discharged by the Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Commissionerate.

The Center manages the entire lifecycle of an Authorized Economic Operator, from processing initial applications and issuing temporary certificates to auditing, upgrading, downgrading, or revoking recognition status.
Authorized Economic Operators receive benefits related to customs procedure simplification and guaranteed service delivery as coordinated by the Center and local teams.
Every customs station must establish an Authorized Economic Operator team to ensure the smooth execution of related activities and provide proper services to recognized entities.
Each team is required to nominate a focal point officer to manage coordination with the central Authorized Economic Operator body.
Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Com: This office is designated to perform the functions of the Authorized Economic Operator Center until the Center is formally established.
During this interim period, its Commissioner and officers hold the authority and representative powers of the Center's Director General and corresponding staff.

Authorized Economic Operator: Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Commissionerate

Logistics Operator: When an irregularity or duty evasion is detected involving a Logistics Operator, their accredited benefits are subject to cancellation.
Despite any suspension of benefits, the relevant customs offices must continue to process the customs-related functions of the entity in the same manner as they would for a non-accredited business.
Authorized Economic Operator: In the event of customs irregularities or tax evasion by an accredited logistics operator, the customs station is required to formally notify the AEO center, the Customs Risk Management Commissionerate, or the Customs Automation branch using the prescribed documentation.

Authorized Economic Operator: The Center is mandated to immediately notify all relevant customs offices regarding the suspension, cancellation, or downgrading of an authorized economic operator's certification.
Notification procedures must follow the specific operational template defined in the relevant appendix of the standing order.
National Board of Revenue: The Customs Automation Branch of the Board is a primary recipient of information regarding the status of entity certifications to ensure system-wide coordination.
Customs Risk Management: The Customs Risk Management Commissionerate must be immediately updated whenever an entity's status is revoked or downgraded to maintain accurate risk profiles.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: The Systems Manager is responsible for updating the customs automation infrastructure based on notifications regarding changes to operator status.

Customs Authority: The Director General of the Center is responsible for forming assessment teams to evaluate the eligibility and criteria for receiving recognition certificates.

When internal expertise is unavailable, the authority is permitted to appoint qualified personnel from other customs, excise, and VAT offices or external organizations, provided the relevant entities are formally notified in writing.
Assistant Commissioner of Customs: An officer holding the rank of Assistant Commissioner of Customs or higher must be appointed to lead each evaluation team.
Assessment Team: Each assessment team must consist of a minimum of three officers tasked with evaluating the eligibility and conditions for recognition certificates.
The team composition must mandatorily include individuals with expertise in information technology and accounting.

National Board of Revenue: The Customs Automation Wing of the National Board of Revenue is responsible for notifying relevant offices regarding the activation of a center recognition certificate.
Customs Automation Wing: This unit is tasked with informing various customs offices and stakeholders about the activation of center recognition certificates following the procedures outlined in the relevant appendix.
Customs Risk Management Commissionerate: This office is to be formally notified by the Customs Automation Wing upon the activation of a center recognition certificate.
Customs House: All customs houses are to be provided with the notification regarding the activation of center recognition certificates.
Customs Station: All customs stations must be informed by the Customs Automation Wing when a center recognition certificate becomes effective.
Systems Manager: The Systems Manager is identified as a key recipient of the notification concerning the activation of center recognition certificates.

member_objects.resolved_text: ১১. সেন্টার স্বীকৃতিপ্রাপ্ত প্রতিষ্ঠান মনোনীত প্রতিনিধিদের কাস্টমস স্টেশনে সহজে প্রবেশ ও কার্যক্রম পরিচালনার জন্য বিশেষ পরিচয়পত্র প্রদান করবে। সেন্টার বিশেষ পরিচয়পত্রের জন্য প্রতিষ্ঠানের মনোনীত প্রতিনিধির নাম, ঠিকানা, জরুরি যোগাযোগ নম্বর ও ই-মেইল, জাতীয় পরিচয়পত্রের কপিসহ আবেদন পেলে তার পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে কাস্টমস স্টেশনে গমনাগমনের জন্য কেন্দ্রীয়ভাবে সেন্টার স্বীকৃতিপ্রাপ্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানের আমদানি/রপ্তানির পরিমাণের ভিত্তিতে প্রয়োজনীয় সংখ্যক মনোনীত প্রতিনিধির জন্য পরিচয়পত্র সরবরাহ করবে। পরিচয়পত্র সরবরাহের ক্ষেত্রে কার্ড প্রস্তুতের জন্য প্রযোজ্য ব্যয় প্রতিষ্ঠানের নিকট হতে আদায় করা যাবে। সেন্টার হতে জারিকৃত পরিচয়পত্র প্রদর্শন করে স্বীকৃতিপ্রাপ্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানের প্রতিনিধি কাস্টমস স্টেশনসহ কাস্টমসের সকল দপ্তরে প্রবেশ করতে পারবে। তবে, দপ্তরের বিভিন্ন স্পর্শকাতর স্থান যেমন, কাস্টমস ভল্ট, সার্ভার ইত্যাদি স্থানে উক্ত কার্ডধারী প্রবেশ করতে পারবে না।

Authorized Representative Identity Card: The Center provides official identification cards to designated representatives of authorized institutions to facilitate their entry and operational activities at customs stations.

The application for such cards requires the submission of specific personal details including contact information and a copy of the national identity document, with the quantity of cards issued based on the institution's import and export volume.
The costs associated with the production of these identification cards are recoverable from the respective institution.
Customs Station Access: Authorized representatives holding the official identity card are permitted to enter customs stations and other designated customs offices for their professional duties.
Access is strictly prohibited for cardholders in sensitive operational zones such as customs vaults and server rooms.

Customs Authority: This directive mandates that customs offices must conduct any necessary investigation or inquiry against recognized institutions within the shortest possible time frame.
Recognized Institutions: These entities are subject to investigations or inquiries conducted by customs offices in accordance with the relevant legal provisions.

member_objects.resolved_text: ১৪. স্বীকৃতিপ্রাপ্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানের ক্ষেত্রে আইনের আওতায় কোন ন্যায় নির্ণয় ও বিরোধ নিষ্পত্তির প্রয়োজন হলে তা সকল কাস্টমস দপ্তর কর্তৃক অগ্রাধিকার ভিত্তিতে নিষ্পত্তি করতে হবে। আপিল নিষ্পত্তির ক্ষেত্রে স্বীকৃতিপ্রাপ্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানকে পৃথক করার ব্যবস্থা রাখতে হবে (যেমন, ইলেকট্রনিক পদ্ধতিতে পৃথক নম্বর বা ম্যানুয়াল পদ্ধতিতে AEO লোগো দেখে অগ্রাধিকার প্রদান) এবং উক্ত পৃথকীকরণের ভিত্তিতে যথাসম্ভব দ্রুততার সাথে আপিল নিষ্পত্তি করতে হবে।

Authorized Economic Operator: In cases involving adjudication or dispute resolution for accredited entities, all customs offices must process these matters on a priority basis.

Customs offices must implement systems to distinguish accredited entities during appeal proceedings, using methods such as electronic flagging or the use of the AEO Accreditation Logo for immediate identification.
Appeals regarding accredited entities must be resolved with maximum speed based on the priority status granted to them.
AEO Accreditation Logo: The logo serves as a practical manual identification method for customs officers to prioritize appeal and dispute resolution processes for accredited operators.
